script: Britain prosecuted the man who won them the war, then apologized decades too late. Alan Turing broke Nazi Germany's Enigma code, shortening the war by years and saving countless lives in the process. He did it in near total secrecy, and for decades the public had no idea what he had actually accomplished. In 1952, British authorities prosecuted him for being gay, then a criminal offense, and forced him to undergo chemical castration instead of prison. He lost his security clearance, his career, and his reputation within two years. In 1954, he died from cyanide poisoning, ruled a suicide by the same government he had saved. Britain didn't formally apologize until 2009, and only issued a royal pardon in 2013, fifty nine years after his death. Britain prosecuted the man who won them the war, and it took nearly sixty years to say sorry.
